title: Rule 1: Total Preservation
teaches: The invariant that the sum of elements remains constant after folding.
visual: Side-by-side comparison: [1, 2, 3, 4] (sum=10) folds to [5, 5] (sum=10). Animated counters show both sums equaling 10. A checkmark appears with 'Total Preserved'.
narration: Crucially, a brisk fold preserves the total sum of the original list. Since we only add existing numbers together without discarding any, the aggregate value remains invariant across folds.

title: Rule 2: Length Reduction
teaches: The structural change: length roughly halves after one brisk fold.
visual: List [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] (length 6) folds to [7, 7, 7] (length 3). An arrow labeled 'Length / 2' connects the two states. Visual emphasis on the halving effect.
narration: Each brisk fold roughly halves the length of the list. This compression property makes brisk folds useful for reducing data size while maintaining its essential numerical sum.
